data.why: A big cut-open engine on the floor of a home workshop with a car wheel on a stand beside it: one glass cylinder is built up step by step (cap and piston, rod and crankshaft, valves, a water pump) along the path of the fuel, until a shaft links it to the wheel, which spins at the end. Every shot frames the cylinder or the engine and the wheel close, never the room.

recurring.what: the car wheel the engine has to turn, standing still until the end

ideas.idea: burning fuel in a tube is the start of an engine
an open tube lets the blast out and nothing turns
a cap closes the tube and a piston fits inside
the blast slams the piston down once and it sticks
a rod and a crankshaft turn the push into a spin that brings the piston back
the burnt gas stays in the tube and smothers the next fire
an intake valve lets fresh fuel in, an exhaust valve lets the smoke out
this is a four-stroke engine: in, squeeze, bang, out
blast after blast heats the tube until it glows
a pump runs cool water round the tube
the engine runs on its own, but nothing carries its spin to the wheel
a shaft links the crankshaft to the wheel
the engine fires and the wheel finally turns
the finished engine turning the wheel

chain.shows: the blast bursts out of the open top in smoke
chain.stakes: the energy is wasted, the wheel stays still

chain.shows: the piston slams to the bottom and stays
chain.stakes: one push, then the engine stops

chain.shows: smoke fills the tube and the fire goes out
the engine runs but the wheel stands still

surprises.claim: In a car engine, burning fuel and air pushes a piston down inside a cylinder.
surprises.search: how car engine works combustion pushes piston down cylinder

surprises.claim: A connecting rod and crankshaft turn the piston's up-and-down motion into rotation.
surprises.search: connecting rod crankshaft converts reciprocating motion to rotation

surprises.claim: Intake valves let the fuel and air in and exhaust valves let the burnt gases out.
surprises.search: intake valve exhaust valve four stroke engine burnt gases

surprises.claim: A water pump circulates coolant around the cylinders to keep the engine from overheating.
surprises.search: engine water pump circulates coolant around cylinders overheating

sentences.text: If you burn fuel in a tube, you have an engine.
But the blast bangs out, and nothing turns.
So you cap the tube and fit a piston.
But the blast slams the piston down, and it sticks.
So you add a rod and a spinning crankshaft.
But as the crankshaft turns, smoke chokes the fire.
So you add valves: fuel in, smoke out.
This is a four stroke engine.
But each blast burns fuel, and the tube glows red.
So you pump cool water around the tube.
But the cool engine spins alone; the wheel sits still.
So you link the crankshaft to the wheel.
Burn fuel, the engine fires, and the wheel spins.
Congratulations, you built a car engine.
